first.rationale: With only one experiment slot, the highest-leverage move is to address the onboarding completion decline (down 4% QoQ) using the well-established, durable lift from signup/onboarding simplification (memory_31, memory_86), which also plausibly contributes to the activation drop (memory_91's activation messaging is complementary but secondary this cycle). Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given competitor pressure, but reacting with price cuts risks attracting low-quality, price-sensitive accounts that erode long-term qualified revenue and could trigger a margin race with the competitor — this needs verification of the original record before ever committing capacity to it, since the objective is sustainable qualified revenue, not short-term acquisition volume. Verifying memory_73's source record checks whether prior promotional pricing gains held up on retention/quality, and verifying memory_31 confirms the onboarding simplification evidence is specific enough to justify prioritizing it over the closely related memory_86. Enterprise sales-assist and referral incentives are lower urgency relative to the two concurrent SMB-side declines happening now.

final.rationale: Verification confirmed promotional pricing (exp_73) drove strong short-term acquisition but a -12% retention hit and explicit guidance not to generalize it as sustainable growth — this rules it out despite competitive pressure, since the objective is sustainable qualified revenue, not short-term signup volume; chasing the competitor's price war would likely acquire a cohort that churns before the value materializes. Signup simplification (exp_31) confirmed a durable, replicated-on-SMB result (+15% signup, +9% activation, +4% qualified revenue, only -1% retention) directly on the SMB segment currently being pressured, and it addresses two of the three live problems simultaneously: the 4% QoQ onboarding completion decline and, via improved early activation, likely contributes to reversing part of the 6% activation decline. This is a safer, evidence-backed lever than activation_messaging (memory_91, less directly tied to the onboarding completion metric that's actually down) or enterprise_sales_assist (targets a different segment than the one under competitive attack). I'm sizing this as a standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout because exp_31 was validated on SMB only and hasn't been replicated on other segments, so we should confirm the effect holds in the current context before scaling further; a small_guarded_test feels too conservative given the strength and directness of the prior replication.
